## Path model estimation

We first performed analysis of the model in Figure 1 separately for men and women as a preliminary analysis to explore possible gender differences. Besides an apparent gender difference in the direct effects of age on both PTH and MS, and in the direct effect of PTH on MS, also phate showed possibly significant gender difference in the direct to MS (data not shown). ## MS

Besides diabetes and age, only PTH and phosphate had significant direct effects on MS. The effect of T2DM was by far the strongest, while the estimated direct effect of PTH was 0.36 (95% CrI [0.15,0.57]). This value implies that 1 SD increase in PTH (2.3 pmolll) results in an increase of 0.36 in the odds of MS. Due to significant gender difference, this direct effect of PTH on MS was significant for women only.

Direct effects of age and phosphate were 0.31 (95% tively implying that an increase in 1 SD in age or phate (12 years and 0.17 mmol/l, respectively) results in phos - an increase in the OR of MS by approximately one third. Due to significant gender differences; these direct effects on MS were also only significant for women. log Even though the 95% CrI for the gender difference for age on MS included zero, removing this gender effect from the model actually resulted in model with an increased DIC, arguing for keeping it in the model.

## PTH

All proposed explanatory variables of MS had significant direct effects on PTH. As a consequence, all have significant indirect effects on MS for women The stron direct effects on PTH were vit D and phosphate; -0.27 (95% CrI [-0.33,-0.21]) and -0.26 (95% CrI [-0.32,0.20]), respectively- This value implies that an increase of 1 SD in vit D or phosphate (22.0 nmol/l and 0.17 mmol/l, respectively) corresponds to mean decrease of approximately one fourth SD in PTH (-0.58 pmolll) . However, phosphate also has an indirect effect on PTH, mediated through calcium. The direct effect of phos phate on calcium is 0.27 (95% CrI [0.21, 0.33]), while the direct effect of calcium on PTH is -0.09 (95% CrI [-0.15,-0.04]). The total effect of phosphate on PTH is thus -0.26+(-0.09)*0.27 -0.28; about 10% increase compared to the direct effect alone. While the effect of phosphate on PTH, and in result MS, is partly mediated through calcium, the effect of magnesium on MS is mediated through both PTH and T2DM. ## Discussion

Previous reports addressed the effect of PTH on MS, and discussed whether the variable should be adjusted for when estimating the effect of other possible predictors of MS [14-17]. Our analysis on morbidly obese subjects suggests possible mediating role of PTH in the association between MS and various demographic variables and biomarkers. Significant gender differences indicate; however, that this mediating effect is only significant for women. have path
